transcript.text: If your tumble dryer seems to run forever without stopping, it usually means one of two things: either the programme hasn't finished yet (some cycles take 2+ hours), or there's an electrical fault keeping the power on. First, check if the drum is actually tumbling. If it has stopped spinning but you still hear a fan running and the lights are on, try pressing 'Pause' or 'Stop'. Does it fully switch off? If not, please unplug it from the wall immediately to be safe. If it does stop when you press Pause, tell me: did the clothes feel damp at the end of that cycle?
it finishes and says End but then the drum keeps turning every couple of minutes if I leave the clothes in. stops when I open the door. clothes are dry

This sounds like the normal 'cool down' or 'anti-crease' phase. Most tumble dryers keep the drum turning gently for a few minutes after the programme ends to prevent your clothes from setting in creases. The fact that it stops immediately when you open the door suggests this is a safety feature (the machine pauses tumbling if the door is opened), rather than an electrical fault. If the tumbling lasts more than 10–15 minutes, or if the drum continues to spin rapidly after you close the door again, that would suggest a problem with the door switch or control board. Otherwise, it is safe to leave them in there for a short while or take them out as soon as they are cool enough.
it carries on for about an hour if I leave them, not just 10 minutes. is that normal? worried its wasting electricity

This uses very little electricity (just a small motor), so you aren't wasting much power. If it still runs for an hour with the door firmly shut and clicks properly into place, then we should check if the door switch is faulty or if there's a control board issue.
the door shuts fine I think. what should I check? I don't know what the door switch is

The 'door switch' is a safety mechanism that tells the machine the door is shut; if it doesn't register as closed, some dryers will keep running or behave oddly. Please unplug the dryer first. Look at the plastic hook on the edge of the door and the slot in the frame where it clicks in. Check if any fluff is blocking it, if the hook looks broken, and listen closely: does it click firmly every time? If it feels loose or doesn't click properly, that's likely the cause.
ok its unplugged. I looked at the door and I can't tell if it clicks. what else could it be?

If the door switch isn't registering that the door is shut (even though it looks fine), the machine may think the door is open and keep running the anti-crease tumbling indefinitely. Alternatively, if the switch is working but the signal isn't getting to the brain of the machine, the control board could be at fault. To help me identify exactly which part might need replacing or how to test it further, I need the make and model number of your dryer. This is usually on a sticker inside the door opening or on the back panel. Do you have that information?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a Beko. I don't know the model number, where do I find it?

The model number is usually found on a white or silver sticker located either inside the door opening (on the frame or rubber seal) or on the rear panel of the machine. It will typically start with letters like 'DH', 'DV' or similar followed by numbers. If you can't see it easily, try looking around the edges of the door frame first.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
I looked round the door edge but can't see a sticker. is it somewhere else?

The model number on Beko dryers is often on a sticker inside the door frame or on the back of the machine; if you can't reach it now, we can troubleshoot without it. Given that the drum runs for an hour after 'End' but stops when you open the door, the most likely cause is a faulty door switch (interlock). This part tells the control board whether the door is shut; if it fails to signal 'closed', the machine may keep tumbling indefinitely as a safety measure. To confirm this, please unplug the dryer and check for continuity across the door switch terminals: press the plunger in and out while testing with a multimeter. If the reading doesn't change from open to closed (or vice versa), that part is likely faulty.
I don't have a multimeter and wouldn't know how to use one. is there anything simpler I can check?

Since you don't have a multimeter, we can't easily test the switch ourselves without taking the machine apart. Based on your description—that it runs for an hour but stops when you open the door—the most likely cause is a faulty door switch (interlock). This part tells the dryer that the door is shut; if it fails, the machine may keep tumbling indefinitely as a safety measure. Because replacing this involves opening the casing and dealing with internal wiring, I recommend calling an engineer to replace the door switch safely.
